summary.headline: Gokaldas Q2 FY27: consolidated EBITDA up 48% YoY and India volumes up 10%, with net debt cut to Rs 429 crore.
summary.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 consolidated income up 13% YoY and EBITDA up 48% YoY, helped by product mix, productivity and a weak prior-year base hit by US tariffs. India business grew 10% YoY against overall Indian apparel exports up 1.2%, and Africa grew 32% YoY. Net debt fell to Rs 429 crore at September 2026 from Rs 553 crore in March 2026. Management said sourcing has lagged consumption in key markets, with early recovery in US and EU imports in August, and tied the next leg of growth to the BTPL merger, new Africa customers from April and the EU FTA.

financial_highlights.change: Q1 was over 44% YoY per analyst
internal target about 75 days for FY

segments.name: India (ex-BTPL)
segments.commentary: Grew 10% YoY in a seasonally weak quarter; capacity utilisation expected near 90% in Q3. Current India capacity about 5.9 million pieces by year-end, with 2-3 new factories targeted next year, each adding about 3.5 million pieces.

segments.name: Africa
segments.commentary: Grew 32% YoY on higher volumes and better realisations; utilisation about 40% per analyst, with management guiding about 85% in Q3. Two new customers (one American, one European) start from April; one ~20-25% customer is being ramped down.

segments.name: BTPL (fabric, pending merger)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue about Rs 170 crore, EBITDA slightly negative; Q3 revenue guided about Rs 225 crore with EBITDA breakeven; Q4 about Rs 250 crore with PBT breakeven targeted. Working capital about Rs 300 crore; about one-third of output consumed by Gokaldas, target 50% by FY29.

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: Currently about 15% of revenue including UK; management aims for about 25% over four to five years.

guidance_outlook: Management expects gradual recovery in sourcing volumes over coming quarters; India volume growth targeted at double digits in FY28, with revenue growth strong from Q3 FY27.

Management is confident of reaching about 10% EBITDA margin within about six months; expects margin upside in H2 from about 1.4% FX benefit (about 0.5% of total revenue) and pass-through of input costs.
Africa: management expects robust growth in Q3-Q4 and at least 28% growth in FY28.
FY27 year-end net debt targeted at Rs 650-700 crore including BTPL (about Rs 300 crore debt) and Rs 80-100 crore cash settlement to BTPL shareholders.
Capex: about Rs 150-175 crore in FY27 and at least Rs 200 crore in FY28; combined FY26-29 capex Rs 450-500 crore.
Effective tax rate expected to be very low for some time after BTPL's accumulated losses (over Rs 600 crore) are absorbed.
BTPL merger completion expected in Q3; NCLT judgment reserved, verdict expected within about 10 days.
EU-India FTA benefits expected to flow only from around end-2027 calendar, as orders are placed four to six months ahead.
capex_capacity: India capacity about 5.9 million pieces by year-end FY27; Bhopal phase 2 (about 3.5 million pieces, about Rs 200 crore revenue) to be fully ramped by FY27 end.

Ranchi: new 1,000-machine factory (about 2,000 machines effectively, about Rs 400 crore revenue) under way; total India revenue capacity about Rs 600 crore from these plus further factories of about Rs 200 crore each.
BTPL revenue capacity about Rs 1,200 crore; about 35% of that assumed to net off as intercompany sales to Gokaldas.
Capex plan: about Rs 150-175 crore FY27, at least Rs 200 crore FY28; combined FY26-29 Rs 450-500 crore.
demand_pricing: US Section 301 final rates effective 24 July 2026 put India on par with Bangladesh, Cambodia, Indonesia and Sri Lanka and about 12.5% vs China and Vietnam; India previously faced about 50% additional duties.
UK-India CETA in force from 15 July 2026, giving India duty parity with Bangladesh and about 12% advantage over China. EU-India FTA expected to be signed soon.
AGOA extended through December 2026 incl. third-country fabric provision; Africa revenue booked largely via UAE.
Aggregate US/EU/UK apparel imports down YTD to August 2026; US and EU imports turned positive in August and US imports reportedly +14% in September per analyst question.
Management says realisations are seasonally higher in Q1-Q2 due to outerwear and winter mix; price increases tied to input cost pass-through.
Management expects customers to shift to shorter lead times and value-seeking behaviour; NRF projects 4.2% US holiday retail sales growth.

qa_highlights.question: Is labour availability constraining growth and how is the company expanding capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Shortfalls are met with migrant labour, expansion is in Central and Eastern India, and the company runs its own training camps from Central India to Arunachal Pradesh. Bhopal and Ranchi are the main expansion sites.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Africa and India margins dip sequentially and when do they recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited seasonally weak Q2 with fixed-cost absorption, and expects margin improvement from H2 via pricing, input pass-through and FX (INR 91 in Q2 vs about 93 in Q3). Management expects about 10% margin within six months.

qa_highlights.question: What are BTPL's revenue, EBITDA and debt trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 revenue about Rs 170 crore; Q3 about Rs 225 crore with EBITDA breakeven; Q4 about Rs 250 crore. BTPL working capital debt about Rs 300 crore, held flat.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Rebate of Duties and Taxes on Exported Products (RoSCTL) be extended and what is the impact?
qa_highlights.answer: RoSCTL is about 3.5% of export revenue (about 1.5-1.55% of total revenue per management); a 50% cut would cost about 1.75% and would be absorbed via pricing and productivity. Discussions with government are ongoing.

qa_highlights.question: Why are creditor days rising and does it raise procurement cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aligned payment cycles with customer credit terms, extending vendor credit; no cost increase seen.

qa_highlights.question: Is Bangladesh's LDC status expiry a risk or opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Bangladesh LDC zero-duty access to Europe expires November 2029 (per management); its loss would shift EU orders to India. Management does not expect a large shift.

risks_watch: Pending NCLT final approval for BTPL merger; SFIO-related allegations under review legally.
Expiry or reduction of RoSCTL (about 1.5-1.75% of revenue) from December 2026.
Customer concentration: one Africa customer (~20-25% of Africa revenue) being ramped down on credit concerns.
Consumer sentiment and inflation in US; retailers shortening lead times may keep imports low even as retail sales rise.
Working capital: about 20 days of incremental working capital tied up in BTPL; target 75 days.
Tax rate trajectory and deleveraging depend on BTPL losses and cash generation; dividend and USD 1 billion revenue timelines not committed.
summary.management_tone: Confident on medium-term growth and margin recovery, but cautious on near-term sourcing; management repeatedly tied upside to FY28 and to clarity on tariffs, oil prices and geopolitics. Some answers were vague on specifics (e.g., exact margin and revenue numbers, RoSCTL outcome).

growth.why: Management guides strong revenue growth from Q3 FY27 and India volume growth at double digits in FY28, backed by Bhopal phase 2 and Ranchi capacity, two new Africa customers from April and BTPL revenue rising to about Rs 225 crore in Q3 and Rs 250 crore in Q4, though no explicit consolidated FY27 revenue growth % was given and the EU FTA benefit is delayed to end-2027.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management is confident of reaching about 10% EBITDA margin within six months, helped by about 1.4% FX benefit (about 0.5% of total revenue) and input cost pass-through, from a seasonally weak Q2 base.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Bhopal phase 2 (about 3.5 million pieces, about Rs 200 crore revenue) to be fully ramped by FY27 end, Ranchi 1,000-machine factory (about Rs 400 crore revenue) under way for Q3, and 2-3 more factories targeted next year; India utilisation expected near 90% in Q3.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.when: Q3 FY27 onward; double digit in FY28
rows.why: India grew 10% YoY vs Indian apparel exports +1.2%, Africa +32% YoY with two new customers from April, and BTPL revenue guided to about Rs 225 crore in Q3 and Rs 250 crore in Q4; management targets double-digit India volume growth in FY28.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation near 90% in India in Q3 with capex guided at Rs 150-175 crore for FY27 and at least Rs 200 crore for FY28, and customer projections needing capex above Rs 200 crore, so a further capex step is already in the plan.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management expects revenue growth to be strong from Q3 FY27 and Africa at least 28% growth in FY28, but gave no explicit consolidated FY27 revenue growth percentage, and sourcing is still lagging consumption.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: RoSCTL (about 1.5-1.55% of total revenue) may be cut by 50% from December 2026, costing about 1.75% of revenue, and US/EU/UK apparel imports were down YTD to August 2026 with the EU FTA benefit delayed to end-2027.

rows.label: BTPL merger completion
rows.why: Merger completion expected in Q3 with NCLT verdict expected within about 10 days; BTPL revenue about Rs 170 crore in Q2 rising to about Rs 250 crore in Q4, EBITDA breakeven in Q3.

rows.label: Net debt to Rs 650-700 crore at FY27 end incl. BTPL
rows.why: Net debt cut to Rs 429 crore in Sept 2026 from Rs 553 crore in March 2026, with FY27 year-end guided at Rs 650-700 crore including about Rs 300 crore BTPL debt and Rs 80-100 crore BTPL settlement.

rows.label: Very low tax rate post BTPL losses
rows.why: BTPL accumulated losses over Rs 600 crore are expected to be absorbed, so the effective tax rate is guided to stay very low for some time.

tone.note: Management was confident on the 10% margin within six months, the Q3 ramp, the BTPL merger and FY28 double-digit India volume growth, but cautious on near-term sourcing and vague on RoSCTL and exact revenue numbers; analysts pushed on RoSCTL, creditor days and Africa customer concentration.
